dedupe_keys.name: high resolution datasets for heat vulnerability assessment in high density urban areas of the netherlands 4tu researchdata

description: Two 5 m GeoTIFF layers for heat vulnerability assessment in dense Dutch urban areas, published on 4TU.ResearchData in January 2025 by Maha Habib Abdelraouf and co-authors. The first is the daily maximum urban heat island effect (UHImax) in kelvin, range 0 to 10 K, for summer 2023 from 1 June, computed with the diagnostic equation of Theeuwes and colleagues for north-western European cities. The second is the sky view factor, 0 for fully obstructed and 1 for open sky, for 2020 to 2022. Coverage: 99 municipalities with more than 1,000 inhabitants per square kilometre, from Amsterdam and Rotterdam to Sittard-Geleen. Format and access: free download under CC BY-SA 4.0, with a README that explains how to regenerate UHImax for other periods. Caveats: the heat island layer is a modelled diagnostic for one summer, not measured temperature. Useful as input to hazard exposure and heat adaptation simulation for public space and buildings; related records are not yet linked.
